notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide and docs/evidence/fullscreenmodal.md at e7ed622. The guide's Sources note was checked on 28 October 2026 on the installed build itself (jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October), so items citing it carry that build. The evidence's 10 October sections (Checked, Sources, Contract, Browser measurements, Accessibility, Limits, on 0.1.78-636f3f5) are replaced where they differ by its c8526ae section (23 October, #232: black surface, 532 px hero, 28 px close shown only with onClose, empty copy defaults, dialog role, heading and focus trap) and its dbe0e02 section (27-28 October, #392 and #393: the trap focuses the scrolling body, the keys scroll it, trapFocus false for a modal shown inside a page). None of the superseded 10 October sentences is used; the four 10 October sentences used here (a block parent sizes it to its content, a wrapped Section stays a white card, context5 is forced with Page type JioPlus as the default, the Animated warning) still hold on the installed source. Installed FullscreenModal.tsx, web-focus-trap.ts and cloneChildrenWithModes still match every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run (the token values were resolved with the package's own resolver): copy props default to empty strings and an empty line isn't rendered; heroHeight defaults to 532 and is the hero region's minimum height with the text anchored to its bottom; the root's surface is body/background under Page type JioPlus and Color Mode Dark, rgb(0, 0, 0), and the hero text is white (29 px, weight 900); heroMedia sits at the root behind the scroll area and the footer, translated by the scroll offset; the body has a 16 px gap and top padding; the footer is a pinned ActionFooter with 41 px bottom padding, and it renders only with primaryActionLabel or footer; the close button renders only when showClose and onClose are both set, 28 px, 12 px from the top and right; the root has role dialog, aria-modal and the headline as its label, and the headline has the header role; with onClose and trapFocus the scroll area gets tabIndex 0 and the trap focuses it first, keeps Tab inside, calls onClose on Escape and returns focus when removed; modes cascade into children through their children props, so a wrapper component that doesn't forward modes leaves its Sections unstyled. No guide sentence is contradicted. One package doc mismatch: heroHeight's doc comment still says it defaults to 420, while the source default is 532, the guide's figure. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode and no other modes (the guide sets none on the modal; Color Mode Light appears only on its In context Profile screen and the States demo's button, both left out). Left out of examples: the body. The guide's body is Sections (Key benefits, a ListGroup of ListItems with IconCapsule leading icons, and Compare plans, a PlanComparisonCard); Section exists only in code and is not part of Coin, and IconCapsule and PlanComparisonCard have no entry in this pack, so no body is composed rather than invent one the guide doesn't show. Also left out: trapFocus false (the guide's setting for previews shown inside its page; a screen keeps the default trap, as In context does), priceText and disclaimer set to empty strings in the confirmation (they repeat the defaults), the ScreenFrame, the playground and its readout, and the States demo's Show the offer button. The hero media example uses a URL string in place of the guide's bank-hero.png asset. Copy is the guide's own (the JioGold SIP offer, the JioFinance+ upgrade offer and the You're all set confirmation). Not recorded: footer, closeOffsetY, style, contentContainerStyle and testID, which the guide doesn't cover (the evidence classes them as developer-only, and the building rules keep style off Coin components), and Page type overrides, which the evidence lists as not shown. avoidWhen is empty: the guide names no situation that calls for another component, and its Don'ts are about configuring the modal, so they are recorded under configuration and accessibility. Not recorded as gaps, per the pack's rules: #232, #392 and #393, all fixed and verified on dbe0e02 (the evidence's Coin gaps list still shows #392 as To do, but its dbe0e02 section replaces it), dark mode, and screen-reader names. The guide's Sources note renders “trapFocus= turns that off”, because the {false} in its JSX text renders nothing; the quote used here starts after it.

evidenceFacts.name: heroHeight
evidenceFacts.description: The hero text region is 532 px tall by default, as in Figma; the package's own doc comment still says 420.

evidenceFacts.name: heroMedia
evidenceFacts.description: A full-bleed background at the root, pinned to the top at the modal's width (height = width ÷ an Image's ratio), behind the hero text, the body and the footer. It adds no scroll height and moves with the scroll.
evidenceFacts.quote: `heroMedia` is now a full-bleed background at the root, pinned to the top at the modal's width (height = width ÷ `ratio`), behind the hero text, the body, and the footer; it adds no scroll height and moves with the scroll.

evidenceFacts.name: showClose
evidenceFacts.description: The close button (28 × 28, 12 px from the top and right) renders only when showClose and onClose are both set.
evidenceFacts.quote: Close: 28 × 28 (Button / Size S), 12 px from the top and right, rendered only when `showClose` and `onClose` are both set.

evidenceFacts.name: onClose
evidenceFacts.description: Shows the close button. On the web, with trapFocus on (the default), a focus trap moves focus inside on mount (to the scrolling body), keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside, calls onClose on Escape, and returns focus to the opener when the modal is removed. Without onClose it is still aria-modal but doesn't take or keep focus.
evidenceFacts.quote: With `onClose`, a web focus trap moves focus inside on mount, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside, Escape calls `onClose`, and focus returns to the opener on unmount.

evidenceFacts.name: trapFocus
evidenceFacts.description: With trapFocus false, a modal shown from the first render leaves focus on the page and Tab passes through it; Escape doesn't close it, and it is still a modal dialog. With the default, one shown at load takes focus.
evidenceFacts.quote: With `trapFocus={false}` Escape doesn't close it (Escape belongs to the trap), and it is still `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`.

evidenceFacts.name: primaryActionLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Empty by default, so there is no footer until a label or a custom footer is given.
evidenceFacts.quote: `primaryActionLabel` empty, so no footer without a label or `footer`.

evidenceFacts.name: headline
evidenceFacts.description: Names the dialog on the web (aria-label) and renders as the heading. Left empty, the modal has no heading and no name.
evidenceFacts.quote: named by the headline (`aria-label`); the headline is an `h1`

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: The modal's modes cascade into its children, through their children props, but not into a component that doesn't forward modes: a Section inside a wrapper component stays a white card with black text.
evidenceFacts.quote: A Section inside a wrapper component that doesn't forward `modes` stays a white card with black text.

evidenceFacts.name: context5
evidenceFacts.description: Always Fullscreen Modal: the modal forces it and modes can't override it. It gives the components in the body and the footer their white-on-dark look.
evidenceFacts.quote: Modes: `context5: 'Fullscreen Modal'` is forced; `Page type: JioPlus` is the default.

evidenceFacts.name: Page type
evidenceFacts.description: FullscreenModal sets Page type JioPlus itself, which gives the white hero text; modes can override it.
evidenceFacts.quote: Modes: `context5: 'Fullscreen Modal'` is forced; `Page type: JioPlus` is the default.

evidenceFacts.name: Color Mode
evidenceFacts.description: The surface is black in every Color Mode. In Dark the hero text drops Color Mode and stays white.
evidenceFacts.quote: In Color Mode Dark the hero text drops Color Mode and stays white.

gaps.text: Figma draws the modal 1228 px tall with a full-height image behind everything; the package gives it its own black surface, so the hero text reads without media, and media you add sits behind the hero and the body.

from.quote: In Figma the modal is 1228 px tall with a full-height image behind everything; in the package it has its own black surface, so the hero text reads without media, and media you add sits behind the hero and the body.
